description: The floating comment indicator *> (ISO §2023:6.2.3.1) - a comment line when it is the first character-string in the program-text area, an inline comment after one or more character-strings - in either reference format. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85's one comment is the fixed one, §1985:IV.7.2.4 'A comment line is any line with an asterisk or slant in the indicator area of the line.', so *> in the program text of a COBOL-85 source is not a comment indicator; §2002:6.1.2 'Floating indicators may be used in fixed-form or free-form reference format.', its table giving *> as 'a comment line when specified as the first character-string in the program-text area' or an inline comment, and §2002:F.2 item 68 'An inline comment is introduced by the two contiguous characters' *>; §2014:6.2.2 carries the same table. Recognized in ONE place, the §2023:6.5 logical conversion in ReferenceFormatProcessor (kb/Work PB1493), which gates it once per compilation, in FIXED form - the only reference format a COBOL-85 source can be written in (free form is itself a 2002 introduction, §2002:F.2 item 58, reached below 2002 only through the documented --source-format free and auto extensions, and the floating indicator is its only comment); the witness is therefore fixed-form.

000100 IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.

000400 MAIN.
000500     DISPLAY "X". *> an inline comment
